8013.d:
Jimi Hendrix is one of the great guitarists in music. As a Generative Artist, he pioneered with electronics, overdriven amplifiers, high volume, gain, he was instrumental in popularizing the previously undesirable sounds caused by guitar amplifier feedback, and used tone-altering effects, like distortion, wah-wah, Uni-Vibe, and stereophonic phasing. 
Jimi Hendrix wrote ‘Castles made of Sand’ in 1967.  Sandcastles are destined to end and stand for the temporary nature of existence, of time slipping away. Each verse in the song contains universal disappointments... All is not lost, as in the last verse a suicidal girl who is "crippled for life," moving her wheelchair to the shore, seems saved by optimistic epiphany. 
This song inspired me to create on 12 watery inkswabs, 12 phantasmagoric castles, in 2nd and 3rd dimensions, zooming out to the sky with 12 Zodiacs, making 1728pc. In Cabalistics (1+7+2+8= 18 / 7+2 = IX  / 1 + (7+2=9) 7 (2+8=0) ) this generates into September 18th 1970, the day Hendrix died.

Landscapes are an inherent part of the self, where often times the self is represented as an anthropomorphic form, self is indeed also a landscape. While the self is usually concentrated in a living form, self is also the infinite. The self dreams its unique dreams, there is nothing that is as this. These are the landscapes that dreams are made of, and in the dream, dreaming of these landscapes. Lived experiences are the seeds for the dream. 8079.d:
The Bandersnatch is a 0° stable color-changing glider reflector (also known as a "glider shifter") discovered by Entity Valkyrie on June 5, 2020 based on a reaction by Martin Grant. The repeat time is 70, slightly less than the syringes repeat time of 78. Since it contains an eater 2, an eater 1, a loaf and four blocks, it is Spartan. The name is taken from Lewis Carrolls The Hunting of the Snark.

The day of its discovery, Goldtiger997 used this reflector to reduce the repeat time of the highway robber. Later that day, Tanner Jacobi used it to reduce the size of the period-70 glider gun, and Adam P. Goucher discovered that the glider produced by the Bandersnatch could be fed into a nearby rectifier to produce an efficient merge circuit. On June 10, Sphenocorona constructed a p143 Bandersnatch loop using two Bandersnatches and two copies of 66P13. On January 3, 2022, iNoMed reduced this to create a bandersnatch loop supported entirely by relatively small still lifes.

Pattern of the Year for 2020.

Rules : 
  1. Start with either a line or a circle from a number of random points in the space.
  2. A line can only spawn a circle at the end. 
  3. A circle can spawn both lines and circles before it completes the full circle.
  4. A circle can sometimes spawn an inner circle.
  5. Smaller elements will spawn randomly along with the lines.

This was inspired by the patterns in Marvel's movie : Eternals. I enjoyed the line growing animation with basic geometry ( line and circle ). Combining this with the rules It generates interesting results.

To add more variety to the rendering, I've added the dash lines in instead of only solid lines. Also the 'lines' consist of thousands of small dots to give it randomness and a bit of texture feeling.

8098.d:
"I Stockpile Dreams With Tragedies" is an experimental generative art piece that is an attempt to highlight some of the inherent contradictions surrounding the discussion of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and it's place as a vehicle for artistic creation, artistic expression and the potential of remuneration for artists.

To the extent possible, the source code is dedicated to the public domain (CC0) and can be used for any purpose, even commercial, by anyone. Third party libraries are used that are not CC0 licensed but have libre/free licensing terms that allow for commercial reuse (please see the LICENSE section for more details).

This work is heavily based on stock art that is available from pay-to-download sites and other artists that copy the style but don't release the art, or the code to generate it, to the community at large.

This work hopes to add to the conversation about examining the reality of the ecosystem that we've developed around digital goods and intellectual property.

8111.d:
Dive deep into economies & ecologies.

Habitats is an artwork+data visualization about the world economy and the thousands of species, whose existence is threatened by our economies.

Created using p5js.

Remaining supply will be burnt on February 1st.

·Data

Each edition is assigned 3-7 countries as well as a group of species. Each country is represented by a circle, while the species group decides the color scheme.

The GDP (PPP) per capita of each country is shown by the size of the circle. Large circles mean a large GDP, and vice versa.

The amount of threatened species is shown by the density of the circle. A very dense circle means few threatened species, and vice versa.

·Interactivity

Habitats adapts nicely to different screen sizes.

Creatures of the Night Roulette our first generative music NFT ever is the result of a collaboration with Miami Reggae Band RasPunk.

With the power of blockchain technology, some coding, and cool music, each minted NFT will be a unique audiovisual experience, generated completely on-chain.

From the musical standpoint the algorithm will at first assembly various tracks which can vary from 4 to 16 in total, the choice will result in different songs each time, that can go from a very subtle composition to a fully loaded & rich result.

All the tracks were carefully curated by Dario Adames (RasPunk’s executive producer & drummer), so every time any possible combination will make sense musically.

Visually the number of tracks is represented by pulsating circles & rotating lines that will also respond to the pattern of the music.

The tracks used for this artwork are part of RasPunk’s first released single, Creatures of the Night, now available on all streaming platforms.

Follow RasPunk on TW/IG @raspunkmusic

The artwork 'Cogito, Ergo Sum' ('I think, therefore I am,' René Descartes) is an artist's exploration of the human nature of thinking. How similar is the way of thinking for all people? How different are the emotional patterns that affect our thought processes, and how are they interrelated? Do this particular moment in time (the time of the work creation) and the particular person (collector) affect the final result (for the visual solution of a piece)?

Some philosophy, some metaphysics, the participation of real people, and the result of the research are 155 works from the 'Cogito, Ergo Sum' collection.

*The collection is based on the @m5alien artist's idea that new art is born in collaboration between artist, algorithm, and collector.

"100 Shirts, Burning" is an experimental generative art piece that attempts to highlight some of the inherent contradictions surrounding the discussion of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and its place as a vehicle for artistic creation, artistic expression and the potential of remuneration for artists.

Controls:

a - toggle animation

, - slow down animation

. - speed up animation

p - pause animation

s - take screenshot

To the extent possible, the source code is dedicated to the public domain (CC0) and can be used for any purpose, even commercial, by anyone.

This work is heavily based on art available from leading on-demand apparel sites that allow for on-demand printing. Ordering even one shirt from an on-demand printing site exceeds the carbon emissions and the energy requirements to mint a single NFT.

This work hopes to add to the conversation about examining the reality of the ecosystem that we've developed around digital goods and intellectual property.

8189.d:
A 8-glider synthesis of Loafer.

Glider synthesis (or glider construction) is the construction of an object by means of collisions of gliders and glider-constructible spaceships. It is generally assumed that the gliders should be arranged so that they could come from infinity - that is, gliders should not have had to pass through one another to achieve the initial arrangement (or else it is considered “not fully functional”). 

Loafer (also the loafer) is a c/7 orthogonal spaceship found by Josh Ball on February 17, 2013. Its name refers to its slow speed and loaf-pushing behaviour.

It is the fifth smallest known spaceship in terms of cell count (after glider, lightweight spaceship, middleweight spaceship and heavyweight spaceship), being tied with some nontrivial flotillae.

Loafer ranked second place in the Pattern of the Year 2013 competition in a belated vote held on the ConwayLife.com forums, behind the Snark.

8199.d:
Piastrelle is the Italian word for tiles, one of the oldest forms used for decorative art. They’ve been treasured for centuries due to their durability and stunning beauty, as embellishing touches both inside and outside of buildings of all types.

Examples of beautiful tile work can be found in mosaics, murals and more from the oldest civilizations to the present day. Ancient Egyptians, Assyrians, Babylonians, Chinese, Romans and Greeks favoured decorative tiles, and nowadays a wealth of amazing and varied floor and wall tile designs exist to suit all tastes.

This artwork attempts to dialogue with the ancient practice of tiles ornamentation, presenting fragments of tiled surfaces from an extinct civilization of the future, which once had their buildings decorated in all its glory.

Please be aware that there may be some pieces missing, not everything will stand the test of time.

layers, squaresize and direction are randomised and create pieces that remind me of spatula technique used in physical abstract artworks.

- as rendering png’s is possible within every state of the loop, every piece is also an artwork generator itself, capable of generating (almost)  limitless outputs.

"There is no language that speaks so powerfully to the mind as that of Nature. It is intelligible both to the young and to the old, to the ignorant and to the learned, to the lisping infant as well as to the hoary age, to the untutored savage of the forest as well as to the most favored votary of science." Language of Flowers, 1834

The artwork takes the form of generative botanical compositions and is based on the Victorian Language of Flowers. At the times natural expressions of feelings were frowned upon and highly discouraged, flowers became a communicational tool conveying one's delicate feelings to another, yet in a socially acceptable manner. For successful translation, the interlocutors resorted to publications that collected meanings for each plant and its presentation in a particular context. The piece is based on a range of dictionaries and generates compositions with messages nature carries this season. The materials were picked and scanned by the author. The generative code was written by @neelts

Tapestry knitting machine is considered to be a prototype of the computer. Over time, computers began to weave again, composing ornaments and plots. A long time has passed since then, and computer carpets are stored in digital museums, forcing the viewer to view their illegible panoramic images. They are like words that were spoken long time ago, like legends about the wars of robots and octopuses that smart vacuum cleaners tell each other.

Ornaments are best viewed in live mode.

Images are generated with customised VQGAN+CLIP Python code.

8233.d:
Introducing the twelfth work by scarecrow

Scorpions perform a courtship ritual that resembles a dance, sometimes known as a promenade à deux (French for "walk for two"). The details vary by species, but if the female shows interest in the male, they typically begin by facing off and holding onto one another's pedipalps, then rotating back and forth together with their tails (technically metasoma) raised above their backs. They sometimes bump their metasoma together without stinging, according to the San Diego Zoo, in a behavior called "clubbing."3﻿

The dance may last anywhere from minutes to hours. At the end of the dance, the male deposits his spermatophore on the ground for the female, then leaves.

NATURAL 04 are generative and animated pieces creating a visual based on a noise. It’s the fourth part of a collection called NATURAL.
The size, position and frequency of lines are generated for each token, along with the color theme.  Movements are generated by a flow based on a noise, it’s different for each views.
You can press spacebar to stop the animation. 
Save a png : open live and `cmd/ctrl + s` 

 Features :
	- Generated grid between 20 and 75 cols and rows
	- Duration between 18 and 24 seconds
	- Fixed length: if the length of each lines is the same or not
	- Length Factor is a value to manage the length of lines linked with the noise
	- Background color :  color randomly get from 1 of 134 color themes
	- Noise : the number of points to create the noise effect on background

Created by Quentin Hocdé, in Brussels (Belgium).

8243.d:
This is a variant of my previous "Treasure of the burning ship"
After some more "treasure hunting" within this fractal, many more visually stunning views were discovered.
There are 29 possible variations in 7 palettes

To allow collectors to also experience the "Chaos Haunting" I do, interactive controls have been added.
Click the mouse on a point to center it.
A/Z for zoom in/out by 2x.
S/X for zoom in/out on the X axis by 2x.
D/C for zoom in/out on the Y axis by 2x.

In interactive mode, resolution is reduced to 512x512 from 2048x2048 to speed up rendering.
If you find anything really nice, you can check the browser console to see the co-ordinates for that view.
I can render a high res version gratis if you want.

Suppose you mapped each view (at a max zoom of 10 trillion) onto each sq. meter of the Earths surface, you'd need dozens of Earths to finish - and yet no two views would match exactly. Mathematically, we could keep zooming in forever and yet keep finding distinct patterns.
